programme: No single module unites the twelve factors. They fall into functionally unrelated families: two HOX patterning factors (HOXD9, HOXA11), an ISWI chromatin remodeler (SMARCA1), a CtBP corepressor (CTBP2) and a TGF-beta-associated corepressor (TGIF1), a DNA-demethylation enzyme (TET1) alongside a nucleotide-excision-repair sensor (XPC) and a PML-body/H3.3-loading factor (DAXX), a p53-pathway activator (DMTF1), a methyl-CpG reader (MECP2), an intestinal bHLH factor (ASCL2), and a membrane-bound myelin transcription factor (MYRF). None of these groupings corresponds to a documented complex or pathway that would plausibly act as a unit in either blood or kidney.
role_in_a: No coherent programme to assign a role to; individual factors have isolated, unrelated roles noted in the record (e.g. DAXX as a reported SARS-CoV-2 restriction factor, MYRF mentioned in a single COVID-19 encephalitis case report), but these do not converge on one process.
role_in_b: No coherent programme to assign a role to; individual factors have isolated roles noted in the record (e.g. TET1 and HOXD9 each linked separately to renal-cancer epigenetic dysregulation), but nothing ties them to the other ten factors as a unit.
shared_axis: None can be written responsibly: there is no process running through most of these factors together, so there is no axis for two diseases to share.
reasoning: The concordant set spans HOX developmental factors, distinct corepressor families, DNA-repair/demethylation machinery, a p53 regulator, a Wnt-associated intestinal factor, and a myelin factor, with no known complex or pathway spanning more than one or two of them at a time. The literature that was retrieved backs single factors in one disease each (DAXX and MYRF in COVID-19; TET1 and HOXD9 in kidney papillary carcinoma) but never links any two of these factors to each other, so there is nothing to build a shared mechanism on.
support: PMID 35508460 — identifies DAXX as a restriction factor for SARS-CoV-2 (disease A only); PMID 35990002 — single case report of a MYRF variant with SARS-CoV-2 infection and neurological illness (disease A only, weak); PMID 32536823 — implicates HOXD9 among methylation-driven genes in papillary renal cell carcinoma (disease B only); PMID 40524239 — epigenetic silencing of CLDN10B, cited for TET1's role in renal epigenetics (disease B only); PMID 26472283 — SDH/FH loss causing 5hmC loss in paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma, cited for TET1 (disease B only, and not papillary RCC itself).
how_to_falsify: Take the six best-supported factors (HOXD9, SMARCA1, CTBP2, TET1, ASCL2, XPC) and check by ChIP-seq/co-IP in a kidney papillary carcinoma line and a SARS-CoV-2-infected blood-cell model whether any pair physically interacts or co-occupies a shared set of target promoters beyond chance; finding a shared complex or overlapping target program between two or more of them would overturn this incoherent call.
caveats: Blood and kidney are compared across 56 patient-group comparisons drawn from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance counts have limited independent replication. Several retained factors (SMARCA1, CTBP2, DMTF1, HOXA11) have no Open Targets association with either disease and no factor-specific literature at all, and known tissue-generic regulators (e.g. ERG, MEF2C, CEBPB) were already screened out, meaning the remaining heterogeneity is not an artefact of missing an obvious master regulator — the factors are simply drawn from unrelated pathways.
